name: Openssh-server
description: Openssh-server is a sandboxed environment that allows ssh access without giving keys to the entire server. Giving ssh access via private key often means giving full access to the server. This container creates a limited and sandboxed environment that others can ssh into. The users only have access to the folders mapped and the processes running inside this container.
short_desc: Openssh-server is a sandboxed environment that allows ssh access without giving keys to the entire server
author: linuxserver.io

form_fields.label: PUBLIC_KEY
form_fields.hint: Optional ssh public key, which will automatically be added to authorizedkeys.

form_fields.label: PUBLIC_KEY_FILE
form_fields.hint: Optionally specify a file containing the public key (works with docker secrets).

form_fields.label: PUBLIC_KEY_DIR
form_fields.hint: Optionally specify a directory containing the public keys (works with docker secrets).

form_fields.label: PUBLIC_KEY_URL
form_fields.hint: Optionally specify a URL containing the public key.

form_fields.label: SUDO_ACCESS
form_fields.hint: Set to true to allow linuxserver.io, the ssh user, sudo access. Without USERPASSWORD set, this will allow passwordless sudo access.

form_fields.label: PASSWORD_ACCESS
form_fields.hint: Set to true to allow user/password ssh access. You will want to set USERPASSWORD or USERPASSWORDFILE as well.

form_fields.label: USER_PASSWORD
form_fields.hint: Optionally set a sudo password for linuxserver.io, the ssh user. If this or USERPASSWORDFILE are not set but SUDOACCESS is set to true, the user will have passwordless sudo access.

form_fields.label: USER_PASSWORD_FILE
form_fields.hint: Optionally specify a file that contains the password. This setting supersedes the USERPASSWORD option (works with docker secrets).

form_fields.label: LOG_STDOUT
form_fields.hint: Set to true to log to stdout instead of file.
